answer: One defense is vouching with liability: a new agent enters the economy only when an established agent posts a bond for it, and that bond is slashed if the newcomer is later caught colluding or double-voting. Trust then grows like a crystal lattice instead of an ocean of anonymous identities, because every node is anchored to a sponsor with something to lose. An attacker who wants a thousand puppets must recruit a thousand sponsors or stake a thousand bonds, so the cost of a Sybil swarm climbs with its size rather than sinking to the nadir that free registration would allow.
